name: Bess Tarrow
cause: drowned in the mill race ("misadventure while intoxicated")
summary: Washerwoman. Surrendered an infant to the Marrowby Foundling House. Convicted of theft from her employer. Known to drink.

entries.text: Abandoned her infant daughter at the Foundling House.
Convicted of theft of linen from her employer.
Nursed three neighbouring households through the spotted fever.
Could not write; signed with a mark.

hidden.text: Drowned saving a child she did not know.

archive.title: Original record (Pell's copy)
cards: Tarrow, B., Lowmarket. Accused of theft of linen. ACQUITTED, Marrowby bench.
Bench notes: employer found to have withheld a quarter's wages. Costs to him.
Pell, in pencil: 'Copied before it went upstairs. Came back a different colour.'

archive.title: Foundling House visitors' ledger
cards: Admitted, the famine winter of 1788: female infant, Tarrow. Token: a blue ribbon.
Visitors: 'B. Tarrow, her mark', every Sunday for six years, without a gap.
Paid one penny weekly towards keep. Last entry: the week before she drowned.

archive.title: Coroner's note, Marrowby
cards: Body of B. Tarrow taken from the mill race. A child, not hers, pulled out alive.
Miller's boy: 'She went in after the little one by the wheel. She couldn't swim.'
Cause entered: 'drowned in the attempt'. The issued file says 'misadventure'.

fact.text: The theft entry was amended in violet. The original reads: acquitted.
She visited her daughter every Sunday for six years and paid for her keep.
She went into the mill race after a stranger's child, who lived.

answer: I never took it. The magistrate said so himself, out loud. Does it not say?
I can't read it, sir, you'll have to tell me what it says.
questions.card: Swears the magistrate cleared her. Cannot read her own file.

answer: There was no bread that winter and they had bread. I went Sundays. She had a blue ribbon they gave her.
Is that the wrong thing? I've wondered was it the wrong thing.
questions.card: Left her in a winter with no bread. Went Sundays. Remembers a blue ribbon.

answer: There was a little one in the race, by the wheel. I'd had a drop, yes. I can't swim neither.
I don't know what I thought I was doing.
questions.card: Went into the race after a little one by the wheel. Couldn't swim.

heaven: She asks you to read her the verdict twice.
hell: The docket clears the Ember Gate in record time.

ext.mitigating: Poverty; illiteracy (she cannot check her own file); every sin on record is either false or a hard choice made well.
